hens_rule_text: Up to 6 hens allowed, but most residential zones (R-125 down to R-50) require a Special Exception approved by the Board of Adjustment before keeping any; only the AGR-1 and AGR-2 agricultural-residential zones allow chickens by right.
permit_notes: A zoning Special Exception from the Board of Adjustment is required in standard residential zones before installing a coop; chickens are allowed outright only in AGR-1/AGR-2 zones.
setback_notes: City guidance states the coop should be at least 30 ft from the nearest residence; not confirmed as the exact zoning-code figure, only as stated on the city's 311 knowledgebase page.
coop_rules: Coop/hen house must be provided for predator protection and kept clean without creating odor or noise nuisance.
zoning_notes: Zoning Ordinance permits chickens by right in AGR-1 (Residential Agriculture) and AGR-2 (General Agriculture); allowed by Special Exception (Board of Adjustment) in R-125, R-100, R-85, R-75, R-65, R-60 and R-50 residential districts.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
